title_en: The Importance of Humility in Prayer
body_ar: ليس للمرء من صلاته إلا ما عقل، ولا يعقل المرء صلاته إلا إذا خشع فيها، ومن هنا كان للخشوع أهمية عظيمة، فعلى المسلم أن يحرص على الخشوع، وأن يعمل بأسبابه ما استطاع، فإن الخشوع أول علم يرفع من هذه الأمة، ولهذا لما كان سلف الأمة أهل خشية وخشوع مكن الله لهم، ورفع قدرهم، وأعلى مكانتهم، وخلد ذكرهم. أحوال الناس في عبادة الله عز وجل: الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى قد خلق الإنس والجن لعبادته، وجعلهم متفاوتين في أداء هذا الحق الذي من أجله خلقوا، فمنهم من يوفق بتوفيق الله سبحانه وتعالى إلى استغلال ما أنعم الله به عليه من العمر والوقت فيما خلق من أجله، وأولئك هم الشاكرون، وقليل ما هم..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* A person has of his prayer only what he was conscious of, and a person is not conscious of his prayer unless he is humbled within it. Hence humility has a great importance, and a Muslim must be keen upon humility and act upon its causes as far as he is able; for humility is the first knowledge to be taken away from this community. It was for this reason that, when the community's forebears were people of awe and of humility, God established them, raised their standing, elevated their rank and made their memory endure.

## The conditions of people in the worship of God, mighty and majestic

Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, created humankind and the jinn for His worship, and made them differ in the discharging of this right for the sake of which they were created. Among them is he who is granted success — by God's granting of success, glorified and exalted is He — in using what God has bestowed upon him of lifetime and of time in that for which he was created; and those are the grateful, and few they are..

flags.context: the organising term of the record, in its title and throughout
flags.note: khushūʿ is the inward stillness and submission of the heart that the limbs then show, and in this record it is tied specifically to the prayer. No single English word carries it: 'humility' alone loses the element of absorbed attention, 'concentration' loses the submission. 'Humility in prayer' is used in the title and 'humility' thereafter, with the synopsis's own gloss — being conscious of one's prayer — left to do the work. Not in the glossary; it should be settled corpus-wide. Note that the record also uses 'خشية' (awe, fear of God) alongside it, and the two are rendered differently so the pair survives.

flags.context: the discharging of the right for which humankind and jinn were created
flags.note: adāʾ here means discharging an obligation owed, not the glossary's technical sense of 'performance in its proper time', which belongs to the law of making up missed acts of worship. The glossary rendering must not be applied here. This is the third instance in this slice of the same trap, after records 654 and 663; the glossary entry would benefit from a warning note.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
'ليس للمرء من صلاته إلا ما عقل' in the synopsis echoes a well-known report; the site does not present it as a quotation and no attribution has been added.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
